title: 4Sum
corePattern: Sorting + K-Sum Reduction with Two Pointers
interviewTips: Ask if quadruplets must be unique and order-independent - sorting plus skip-duplicates is expected.
Mention 32-bit overflow explicitly: cast sum to long / long long before comparing to target.
Discuss pruning with min/max possible sums and how solution generalizes to k-Sum recursion.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Enumeration
approaches.intuition: Check every combination of 4 distinct indices and keep those summing to target, deduplicating by sorted canonical form.
approaches.theory: There are C(n,4) index quadruples. Exhaustive search is correct by definition. Two different index sets with same values map to same sorted tuple, so inserting sorted tuple into a hash set removes duplicate value-quadruplets while preserving all distinct ones.

timeComplexity.explanation: C(n,4) = O(n^4) quadruples checked, each needs O(1) sum plus sorting 4 elements for dedup key.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Hash set stores m unique quadruplets; output size m. No sorting space. Worst case m = O(n^4) if all zero.

steps: Enumerate i<j<k<l, e.g. indices (0,1,2,3): 1+0-1+0=0 -> sorted (-1,0,0,1) added
Dedup via set ensures same values from different indices stored once

edgeCases: All duplicates e.g. [0,0,0,0,0] target 0 returns single [0,0,0,0]
Large values near 1e9 need 64-bit sum to avoid overflow

approaches.name: Approach 2: Sort + Double Loop + Two Pointers
approaches.intuition: Sort array, fix first two numbers with loops, then solve remaining 2Sum in O(n) with left/right pointers moving by sum comparison.
approaches.theory: Sorting makes 2Sum on subarray nums[j+1..n-1] solvable with two pointers because if sum < target we must increase left, if sum > target we must decrease right. Skipping equal neighbors for i, j, left, right guarantees each distinct value quadruplet is emitted once. Early min/max sum pruning with smallest/largest possible partners safely breaks or continues loops.

timeComplexity.explanation: Sorting O(n log n) plus O(n^2) pairs (i,j) each scanned once by two pointers O(n). Dominant term O(n^3).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only pointers and result list; sorting uses O(log n) stack in most languages. Output holds m quadruplets.

edgeCases: Duplicate-heavy input e.g. [2,2,2,2,2] target 8 returns one quad via skip logic
Negative target with all positives pruned early by break
